versions.changelog:
- Introduced a new prebuilt scripts library (`scripts/`), providing ready-to-use code primitives for high-frequency or system/API tasks, improving execution speed and reducing LLM token usage.
- Added 18 utility scripts covering functions like file management, clipboard, networking, data processing, database and archive handling, format conversion, image processing, QR code generation, and more.
- Published a comprehensive command reference: `references/command_reference.md`, documenting all prebuilt script capabilities.
- Updated documentation to distinguish between LLM-dynamic and prebuilt-script primitives, and to explain when to use each.
- No breaking changes; core concepts, workflow, and existing capabilities remain intact.

Initial release of cogniexec — a cognitive execution skillset combining cognition and automation.

- Integrates two main layers: cognitive suite (thinking toolkit) and execution framework (code/action automation).
- Uses an orchestration engine to unify all operations—cognitive, code, tool, plugin—into composable atomic steps for complex workflows.
- Features a task router that automatically determines the best layer(s) and execution flow for any user request.
- Provides four universal cognitive operation codes: direct usage, improvement, transfer, and construction.
- Automates code generation, tool calls, and script execution using LLM and command tools, with built-in safety measures.
- Supports multi-step, cross-layer, and mixed tasks with dynamic planning, error recovery, and human-readable summaries.
